_comment: Auction figures reported independently of us, used to check our parse against
the outside world rather than against itself.
Everything else in this repository is derived from CBK's own PDFs, which means
a systematic misread has nothing to collide with — the archive would agree with
itself all the way to a wrong answer. That is not hypothetical: a bid-to-cover
computed from a partial numerator reported Kenyan auctions as persistently
undersubscribed when the published record says they are persistently
oversubscribed, and no test caught it because every test read the same data.
These figures come from Kenyan financial press reporting on CBK's results.
They are recorded ONLY to verify what we parsed. They are never ingested,
never shipped, and never fill a gap: a figure we cannot read from the source
PDF stays missing. Borrowing someone else's transcription would trade a
visible hole for an invisible dependency.
Amounts are KES billions, as the press reports them.
Add entries as reporting is found; each one is a place a silent regression
would now be caught.
WHY THE 2017 COLUMN-SHIFT AUCTIONS ARE NOT HERE — a deliberate omission,
not an oversight, recorded so it is not helpfully corrected later.
Four two-bond auctions published wrong bids for months — 27-03-2017,
24-04-2017, 22-05-2017 and 18-12-2017. An indented header discarded the
first value column, so each first bond took the second's figure and the
second took the auction total:
The correct values are therefore known, and a fifth file (22-12-2014) leaks
a label figure for a different reason — it carries one bond, so no shift of
this shape is possible there.
They are known BECAUSE WE READ THEM OFF THE SAME CBK PDF. Putting them in
this file would make the one non-circular test in the repository circular:
it would check our parse against our own reading of the identical document,
which is precisely the failure this fixture exists to prevent. An entry here
must come from someone who reported the auction independently of us.
Those four files are guarded instead where the guard belongs — in
backend/scrapers/test_auction_results.py, by a fixture reproducing the
indented layout and a mutant that reproduces the exact published wrong
values when value_start_x is reverted. That pins the parse of a document
shape rather than a borrowed transcription. If Kenyan press reporting on
these 2017 auctions is ever found, it belongs here and is welcome.
